QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_1

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (Chartered Accountant SIA) has been engaged by Antyodaya Seva Sangh, an NPO listed on NSE-SSE, to conduct the Annual Impact Report assessment for FY 2024-25. The NPO runs four programmes - watershed management, women SHG training, slum housing repair and rural cataract camps - each falling under a different SAS thematic area. Under the SAS Framework, what is the PRIMARY obligation of the SIA when scoping a multi-activity engagement?

answer.text: Assess only the programme with the largest rupee outlay and extrapolate findings across the others to save engagement time
Combine all four programmes under a single consolidated SAS thematic area selected by the Responsible Party (NPO management)
Apply the relevant SAS thematic area to each programme according to its activity, while ensuring the overall assessment and reporting follow the SAS Framework
Sub-contract the non-core programmes to other SIAs and limit the engagement letter to one programme of the SIA's choice

explanation.text: The Logic: The SAS Framework provides the general guidance for SIA engagements, and the SAS series lists thematic areas (such as SAS 100 for hunger, poverty, malnutrition and inequality, and other SAS standards for the other themes). Each programme should be assessed under the SAS thematic area that fits its activity, while the overall assessment and reporting follow the SAS Framework. Option C captures this correctly. The Trap: Option A drops most of the engagement scope; Option B lets the Responsible Party choose the standard, which is the SIA's call based on the activity; Option D walks away from accepted engagement responsibilities. Note: For a multi-thematic engagement, map each programme to its applicable SAS thematic area and apply the SAS Framework's reporting and assessment requirements to the engagement as a whole.
